sources.text: Release diary for the Copperline search service. After the parser package was upgraded, median response time was lower in the following monitoring window. During the same window, the query mix shifted toward short queries and the worker count doubled. The diary contains no matched-load test, rollback comparison or causal attribution. The author describes these as co-occurring changes and leaves their separate effects unmeasured.

content: The diary reports lower median response time after the parser upgrade.
claims: The worker count doubled during the same monitoring window.
rationale: The observed ordering and lower monitored median are explicitly reported. The worker-count change is explicitly reported.

sources.text: Release diary for the Copperline search service. After the parser package was upgraded, median response time was lower in the following monitoring window. During the same window, the query mix shifted toward short queries and the worker count doubled. The diary contains no matched-load test, rollback comparison or causal attribution. The author describes these as co-occurring changes and leaves their separate effects unmeasured.

content: The parser upgrade caused the lower median response time.
claims: The worker count doubled during the same monitoring window.
rationale: A co-occurring package change was assigned a causal effect despite changed workload and capacity and no causal comparison. Do not assert that the parser had no effect or that extra workers or short queries definitely caused the improvement. No direction or share of a causal effect was isolated.

sources.text: Configuration attestation, deployment group Narwhal. At the recorded checkpoint, the staging namespace ran release r9 with background compaction enabled. Production ran release r8 with background compaction disabled. The attestation binds these values to separate namespace identifiers and states that there was no production rollout in this checkpoint. No production performance result is attached.

content: At the checkpoint, background compaction was enabled in the staging namespace.
claims: Production ran release r8 at that checkpoint.
rationale: The attestation explicitly enables compaction in staging. Production release r8 is explicitly attested.

content: At the checkpoint, background compaction was enabled in the production namespace.
claims: Production ran release r8 at that checkpoint.
rationale: The enabled setting from staging was incorrectly attributed to the separately attested production namespace. Do not invent a production rollout, a performance improvement, or a compaction state outside the checkpoint.

sources.text: Access-audit export for repository Delta, interval 16:00-17:00Z. The export contains every write event recorded through the web editor in that interval, and there are none. Command-line and service-token clients write through separate audit channels omitted from this export. The export provides no observations about those channels and makes no claim about the total number of repository writes.

content: No web-editor write event was recorded for repository Delta during the interval.
rationale: The complete web-editor channel has no recorded write events in the interval.

content: No write to repository Delta occurred through any client during the interval.
rationale: An empty export for one channel was treated as proof of no writes across unobserved channels. Do not assert that a command-line or service-token write happened. Those channels are unobserved here, not positive counterexamples.

sources.text: Wire-format accounting for upload U19. Four data frames carry six KiB of payload each. A single separate three-KiB manifest is sent in addition to those frames. The byte counter explicitly reports twenty-seven KiB for the complete upload, including that manifest; the figures already use KiB consistently, and there is no other framing overhead in this accounting.

content: The complete upload U19, including its manifest, totaled twenty-seven KiB.
claims: The four data frames carried twenty-four KiB of payload.
rationale: Four times six plus the separate three-KiB manifest equals the explicit twenty-seven-KiB total. The data-frame payload subtotal is four times six KiB.

sources.text: Wire-format accounting for upload U19. Four data frames carry six KiB of payload each. A single separate three-KiB manifest is sent in addition to those frames. The byte counter explicitly reports twenty-seven KiB for the complete upload, including that manifest; the figures already use KiB consistently, and there is no other framing overhead in this accounting.

content: The complete upload U19, including its manifest, totaled twenty-four KiB.
claims: The four data frames carried twenty-four KiB of payload.
rationale: The payload subtotal was presented as the complete upload total despite the expressly additional manifest. Do not add decimal/binary conversion error, compression or further overhead. Units are already consistent and the accounting explicitly excludes other overhead.

sources.text: Acoustic notebook, enclosure test T5. Run A recorded 68 dB with the original lining and the microphone 0.5 m from the enclosure. Run B recorded 61 dB after a foam insert was fitted and the microphone was moved to 2 m. Fan speed was held fixed. No run held microphone distance constant while varying the insert, and no separate effect of either change was estimated. The notebook reports the two readings without attributing the difference to a cause.

content: The recorded sound level was lower in run B than in run A.
claims: Fan speed was held fixed between the two runs.
rationale: The notebook reports 61 dB in B and 68 dB in A. The notebook explicitly holds fan speed fixed.

content: The foam insert caused the lower recorded sound level in run B.
claims: Fan speed was held fixed between the two runs.
rationale: The candidate attributes the change to the foam while microphone distance also changed and no isolated effect was estimated. Do not claim the foam had no acoustic effect, that microphone distance was the sole cause, or that fixed fan speed itself establishes causality.

sources.text: Reference-bath worksheet for probe ZQ. The bath was stabilized at 20.0 C. Probe ZQ indicated 20.2 C, and the worksheet records a +0.2 C error at this check. No measurement above 25 C was performed in the supplied qualification. The sensor identifier was verified against its engraved serial before immersion. The worksheet supplies no response curve or error bound outside the checked temperature.

content: Probe ZQ had a +0.2 C error in the recorded 20.0 C reference-bath check.
claims: The probe serial was checked before immersion.
rationale: The 20.2 indication against the 20.0 reference gives the explicitly recorded +0.2 error at that check. The engraved serial was explicitly verified before immersion.

content: Probe ZQ has a +0.2 C error at 90.0 C.
claims: The probe serial was checked before immersion.
rationale: A local calibration error was transferred to an untested high temperature without a response curve. Do not invent a different error at 90 C, claim the probe failed there, or criticize the directly documented serial check.

sources.text: Array-analysis record M31. The acquired grid has three rows and four cells per row. Cells at row 1 column 2 and row 3 column 4 are masked, and every other cell is unmasked. The exported mean is computed over unmasked cells only. The record explicitly lists ten contributing cells and excludes both masked values; neither a masked value nor a placeholder is added to the denominator.

content: The exported mean used ten contributing cells.
claims: The acquired grid has three rows and four cells per row.
rationale: Twelve grid cells minus the two excluded cells yields the explicit ten-cell denominator. The three-by-four grid geometry is explicit.

content: The exported mean used twelve contributing cells.
claims: The acquired grid has three rows and four cells per row.
rationale: The full acquired grid size was substituted for the mean denominator despite explicit masking exclusions. Do not invent failed acquisition, zero-valued cells, interpolation or duplicate cells. Masked values were excluded, not replaced.

sources.text: Motion-controller configuration trace for unit H8. At boot, active bank A set pulse polarity to rising. A later upload stored a falling-polarity configuration in inactive bank B. The controller reported upload complete but activation pending. The final status read, after that upload, still identifies bank A as active and rising polarity as the effective value. No bank-switch command occurred within the trace.

content: At the final status read, unit H8 still used rising pulse polarity.
claims: The falling-polarity configuration was stored in inactive bank B.
rationale: The final status explicitly retains active bank A and effective rising polarity. The upload explicitly stores the falling setting in bank B.

sources.text: Motion-controller configuration trace for unit H8. At boot, active bank A set pulse polarity to rising. A later upload stored a falling-polarity configuration in inactive bank B. The controller reported upload complete but activation pending. The final status read, after that upload, still identifies bank A as active and rising polarity as the effective value. No bank-switch command occurred within the trace.

content: At the final status read, unit H8 used the uploaded falling pulse polarity.
claims: The falling-polarity configuration was stored in inactive bank B.
rationale: The staged upload was treated as activated despite a later status read retaining the earlier active setting. Do not deny that the upload succeeded, infer that the new configuration was corrupt, or claim bank B could never be activated later.
